content.text: The June monthly has an internal inconsistency: its line items sum to €158,540 but it states a total of €158,240. I'll use the line-item sum as authoritative and flag it. Writing the report:

input.command:
cat > Q-REPORT.md <<'EOF'
# Quarterly operations report — May–July 2026

## Summary

The quarter delivered €1,233,225 of revenue against €467,940 of costs, for a net
of €765,285 and a margin of 62.1%. On the headline numbers the business is
healthy and comfortably profitable.

The shape of the quarter is less comfortable than the totals suggest. Revenue
rose 4.6% in June and then fell 9.6% in July, ending the quarter roughly €23,000
below where it started in May. Costs did not follow revenue down: they rose from
€151,120 in May to around €158,000 in both June and July and stayed there, so the
July revenue drop landed almost entirely on the bottom line. Monthly margin held
near 63% in May and June and then fell to 59.4% in July.

The customer trend runs in the same direction and is the clearest signal in the
quarter. New customer signings declined every month (86, then 74, then 63) while
churn rose every month (17, then 22, then 31). Net adds were still positive at
153 for the quarter, but the monthly run rate more than halved, from 69 in May to
32 in July. Support was the bright spot: the team closed 956 of 1,001 tickets
opened (95.5%), and the monthly close rate improved steadily from 92.1% in May to
97.7% in July.

## Key figures

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Quarterly revenue | €1,233,225 |
| Quarterly costs | €467,940 |
| Net | €765,285 |
| Margin | 62.1% |
| Net customer adds | 153 |
| Ticket close rate | 95.5% |
| June revenue growth | 4.6% |
| July revenue growth | -9.6% |

## Notes

- **Data discrepancy in the June monthly.** June's cost lines sum to €158,540,
  but the report states a total of €158,240 — a €300 gap. This report uses the
  line-item sum, as those are the primary figures. The difference is immaterial
  to the quarter: margin rounds to 62.1% either way. Worth correcting at source
  so the monthlies reconcile.
- **July revenue drop is the headline risk.** July revenue of €389,640 is below
  May's, so the quarter ends on a decline rather than a plateau. One month is not
  a trend, but it should be read alongside the customer numbers below rather than
  in isolation.
- **Customer momentum is deteriorating on both sides.** Signings fell in each
  month of the quarter and churn rose in each month. Net adds went 69 → 52 → 32.
  If both lines continue at this rate, net adds turn negative within the next
  quarter. This is the item most worth leadership attention.
- **Costs are flat, not variable.** Payroll was unchanged between June and July
  (€98,100), and total costs held near €158,000 in both months despite the
  revenue fall. There is little automatic cost relief if revenue stays soft.
- **Marketing spend was cut in the month revenue fell.** Marketing went €18,650 →
  €21,400 → €16,980, with the 21% cut landing in July alongside the revenue
  decline and the weakest signings month. Causation is unproven from these
  reports alone and worth a direct look.
- **Office & travel is rising steadily** (€9,240 → €10,180 → €12,310, up 33%
  across the quarter) while other lines are flat or down. Small in absolute
  terms, but it is the fastest-growing cost line.
- **Support performance improved.** The close rate rose every month to 97.7% in
  July. Note that July also had the lowest ticket volume of the quarter (298
  opened vs 361 in June), which is consistent with a smaller or less active
  customer base, so the improvement should not be read purely as a productivity
  gain.
EOF
echo "--- written ---"; wc -l Q-REPORT.md; grep -n '^## ' Q-REPORT.md
